perPromptChanges.prompt: utilize @ui-mockup to create a new revamped version of the app. keep it as close as the the design as you can.
perPromptChanges.response:
I'll look at the mockup and current app first.

Mockup understood. Now current app.

Full picture. Building revamp now.

Now design system — retheme `index.css` to the mockup's cream/ink palette.

Now the header + fullscreen menu (new component from mockup).

Now the hero — tiled logo backdrop, illustration, giant wordmark.

Now About, Tour, Services, OtherProjects, Social, Footer.

Now wire up the page, header placement, and restyle the remaining routes.

Now build and typecheck.

Build clean. Let me run the dev server and check it in the browser.

Hero matches. Scrolling through the rest.

Now let me look at the rest of the page.

Blog page inherits the theme, but its action buttons lost the pill shape. Fixing.

Revamp done. Verified in browser, build clean, no console errors.

**Design system** (`src/index.css`, `tailwind.config.ts`)
- Dark neon → cream paper `#EFEDE8` + ink `#0A0A0A`. Strictly monochrome, ink is the only accent.
- Orbitron/Inter → **Archivo Black** (display) + **Archivo** (body). Bengali face kept.
- Radius scale flattened to 0. Buttons are pills (`.btn-hero` solid, `.btn-secondary` outline). Glitch/glow/gradient effects deleted; `.album-card` is now a hairline panel, `.section-heading` uppercase clamp.
- shadcn tokens retargeted, so every `ui/*` component inherits the palette.

**New**
- `SiteHeader.tsx` — sticky blurred bar, desktop nav, hamburger → fullscreen menu with Listen/Booking (body scroll lock + Esc).
- `ReleaseSheet.tsx` — mockup's fullscreen release panel: cover, badge pills, tracklist, streaming pills. Added a **Read the story** link → `/blog/:slug` so the SEO blog routes stay reachable.
- `lib/links.ts`, `lib/release-format.ts`.

**Rewritten** — Hero (tiled logo wallpaper + radial fade, `logo-trim.png` illustration, giant wordmark), LatestReleases (dense cover grid, all 10 records, opens sheet), About, Tour (compact row list + newsletter), Services, OtherProjects, Social, Footer, NotFound, LanguageDropdown. BlogPost retyped to the same language with its own minimal header.

**Two calls to flag:**
1. Mockup renders no Services section, though its script carries the full SERVICES data. Dropping a real section felt like silent scope loss, so I kept Services, styled in the same idiom, between Tour and Other Projects. Say the word and I'll cut it.
2. Mockup's release cards open a modal instead of navigating. Kept the modal for fidelity, plus the story link so `/blog/:slug` isn't orphaned. `showAllReleases` custom event is gone — every release is always shown, as in the design.

Unverified: mobile widths. `resize_window` reported success but the viewport never changed (window is fullscreen), so I checked desktop only. Layout is the mockup's own mobile-first responsive CSS, but the hamburger overlay hasn't been exercised at a real narrow width.

perPromptChanges.response:
Right — real URLs beat a modal for SEO. Card → `/blog/:slug`, and the blog page gets the sheet's layout.

Rewriting the blog page around the sheet's layout, then pointing cards at it.

Now hash links (`/#releases`) need scroll handling on the home page.

Narrow window now — good, mobile verifies too. Clicking a card.

Navigation works. Landing scroll position is off, though — fixing that properly at the router level.

Done. Modal removed — album cards are real links now.

**`LatestReleases.tsx`** — each card is a `<Link to="/blog/:slug">` (hover label now reads "Read"). `ReleaseSheet.tsx` deleted.

**`BlogPost.tsx`** — rebuilt so the blog page *is* the sheet, just at a crawlable URL:
- Masthead mirrors the popup exactly: cover art left, `RELEASE` eyebrow, badge pills (year · format · genre · duration), display title, description, tracklist, Listen pills — all above the fold.
- Below it, an `<article>` carrying the indexable copy: the story paragraphs, assets, video, credits, recording notes, lyrics — all restyled to hairline panels and `eyebrow` section labels.
- Header back-link now goes to `/#releases`; the tracklist moved up into the masthead (it was duplicated further down).

**SEO gains beyond the URL itself:** each release already had `releaseSeoTitle`/`description`/`keywords` + `MusicAlbum` JSON-LD, and `scripts/seo-build.mjs` prerenders a static `<head>` per route — the build confirms `prerendered 10 release pages, sitemap has 11 URLs`. Every one of those pages is now reachable by a crawlable in-app link instead of a JS-only modal, and each carries an `<h1>` with the release title plus real body copy.

**Two supporting fixes:**
- `ScrollToTop.tsx` mounted in the router — route changes were inheriting the previous page's scroll offset, landing you mid-article. Uses `behavior: "instant"` because the global `scroll-behavior: smooth` was animating (and sometimes stranding) the jump.
- `section[id] { scroll-margin-top: 68px }` so `/#releases` anchors clear the sticky header.

Verified at mobile width: card → `/blog/dim-out-the-lights` lands at top with the right per-release `<title>`, and "All Releases" returns to the grid. Build, typecheck, lint clean. Desktop two-column masthead is the same markup that rendered correctly earlier — the browser stopped honoring resize requests, so I couldn't re-shoot it wide.

Your crop isn't a font — it's hand-lettering drawn into `mim-al-logo.png` (sits under the chin in the artwork), so no exact match exists. Permanent Marker was the closest available in the same medium.

**What changed:**
- `index.css` — loads Permanent Marker; new `.font-hand` utility with a Bengali override (`Noto Sans Bengali` 700, since Permanent Marker has no Bengali glyphs).
- `tailwind.config.ts` — `font-hand` family added alongside `font-display`.
- `.section-heading` → hand face. Dropped the `-0.02em` tracking and raised line-height to 1.06 — marker glyphs have irregular sidebearings and negative tracking made them collide.
- Hero wordmark → hand face, clamp trimmed `18vw→15vw` (max 180px→152px) because Permanent Marker is much wider than Archivo Black and was overrunning at the old size. Same reason the 404 headline and blog release title got slightly smaller clamps.
- Blog page: release `<h1>` and the closing "Ready to Experience the Music?" now hand face, matching home-page headings.

**Deliberately left in Archivo Black:** header/footer wordmark, nav and menu links, release card titles, service titles, venue names, all small caps labels and buttons. Permanent Marker has one weight and no small-size legibility — the hand face stays a display accent, per the scope you picked.

The wordmark now sits directly under the illustration and reads as part of the same drawing. If it's too wide or too slanted next to your reference, Amatic SC is a one-line swap in `tailwind.config.ts` + the `@import` — it's narrower and upright, but much lighter.

perPromptChanges.prompt: are you able to make the blogs more enriched with lyrics and other details so i can have more SEO
perPromptChanges.response:
Lyrics I can't invent — and scraping them off a lyrics site is both unreliable and a copyright problem. Everything *else* that drives SEO I can do now. Let me check the current gaps first.

Two much bigger SEO holes than lyrics: **all 11 pages serve the identical `<title>` and description**, and there's **no sitemap**. Let me verify and gather real facts before writing.

Now I have real data. Enriching the release entries with verified metadata:

Now the SEO head component — this is the biggest win, since every page currently serves an identical `<title>`.

Now the SEO helpers that build titles, descriptions and schema.org JSON-LD from a release:

TypeScript is inferring conflicting literal types from the heterogeneous JSON — this is also the root of that pre-existing `LanguageContext` error. Let me type the content properly and fix both.

Now the homepage `<Seo>` and a build-time sitemap + prerender, so crawlers actually receive the per-page tags:

Album art isn't landing in `og:image` — the hashed filenames live in the JS bundle, not `index.html`. Reading the assets directory instead:

Every release page now shares with its own album art. Verifying the rendered pages in the browser:

Ten unique titles where there was one. Now checking the tracklist and credits render:

One more surface — `llm.txt` feeds answer engines. Adding the verified detail there:

Build clean, lint clean, no console errors.

## What I did

**The lyrics — I need them from you.** I can't write your lyrics, and pulling them off Genius/Musixmatch would be both unreliable and someone else's copyrighted transcription. Paste them and I'll drop them in; `lyrics` fields are already wired and the section renders automatically.

Everything else is done, and I found two problems bigger than the lyrics.

### Every page was serving the same `<title>`

All 11 pages shipped `Mim Al Music` + the same description. Google saw one page. Now:

```
By Any Means — MIM AL Single (2026)
MIM AL — Self-Titled EP (2026) | SHIMMER, ROSE, IN A WORLD
Odd Directions — MIM AL Single (2026)
...10 unique titles
```

New `Seo.tsx` sets per-route title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter + JSON-LD. But a client-rendered SPA only gets that *after* JS runs — social crawlers and answer engines never see it. So `scripts/seo-build.mjs` runs post-build and writes a real static `dist/blog/<slug>/index.html` per route with the tags baked into the head. Vercel serves those from the filesystem before the SPA fallback, so crawlers get real HTML and users still boot the same React app. No config, no new dependency.

Each page also now shares with **its own album art** instead of a generic image.

### No sitemap existed

Same script generates `sitemap.xml` from `content.json` (11 URLs, `lastmod` from real release dates), and `robots.txt` now points to it. Also fixed `og:image` in `index.html`, which pointed at `/src/assets/mim-al.jpg` — a dev-only path that 404s in production, so link previews have been broken.

### Enriched blogs with verified facts

Pulled real metadata from Spotify + the iTunes API — nothing invented:

- **Tracklist section** (EP): SHIMMER 6:04, ROSE 4:16, IN A WORLD 4:15
- **Credits section** with linked JazzPizza, self-released + ℗ line
- **Badges**: year, genre, runtime, track count
- Genres (Rock / Alternative / Metal), exact ISO dates, backfilled onto older releases too
- Blog copy rewritten 3→5 paragraphs, cross-linked between releases (internal links are real SEO weight)
- `MusicAlbum` / `MusicRecording` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD per page, with ISO-8601 durations

**Two facts worth knowing:** ROSE shipped as its own single on 2026-04-04, a month before the EP — it's the lead single, now written into the EP post. And Odd Directions is 2:34 on Apple but 2:31 on Spotify; I used Apple's exact millisecond value throughout.

### Also fixed

That pre-existing `LanguageContext.tsx` TS error is gone — root cause was TypeScript inferring conflicting shapes from the three JSON files. A proper `Release`/`SiteContent` type in `src/types/content.ts` fixed it and gave the new SEO code something real to type against. Only the unrelated `ExcelDownloader` CDN-import error remains.

**Still open:** lyrics (paste them), YouTube Music URLs, and `mim-al-logo.png` is renamed but unused.
